summary: TechCrunch reports that TwitchCon 2023 in Las Vegas was a clear improvement over the overcrowded 2022 San Diego event, helped by Twitch allowing simulcasting and CEO Dan Clancy's visible engagement with streamers. But attendees widely disliked Las Vegas for its cost, lack of walkability, 21+ venues, overstimulation and scarcity of casual "third places". Twitch's CMO confirmed next year's North American convention will not be in Las Vegas.
one_line: TwitchCon 2023 won praise for rebuilding streamer trust, but attendees broadly criticized Las Vegas as expensive, inaccessible and poor for community gathering.
key_facts: Twitch opened TwitchCon 2023 by announcing that it now allows simulcasting, so streamers can stream on multiple other platforms at the same time.
Dan Clancy, Twitch's president since 2019, took over from co-founder Emmett Shear earlier in 2023, ending Shear's 16-year tenure as CEO.
Streamer Jakenbake described Clancy after meeting him at TwitchCon 2022 as "out of touch with what streamers need and want."
Lowco proposed to her girlfriend onstage during the opening ceremony and said Clancy engaged with streamers all weekend.
This was the first North American TwitchCon held outside California since Twitch's inaugural convention in 2015.
Rachel Delphin, Twitch's chief marketing officer, confirmed next year's convention will not be in Las Vegas but did not disclose the location.
TwitchCon 2022 in San Diego was criticized for overcrowding, tight hallways and inaccessibility for attendees using mobility aids, who were nearly trampled by fans swarming popular streamers.
The Las Vegas Convention Center is located at the end of the Strip, and the author paid $37 for one 10-minute rideshare; Uber waits ranged from five to 30 minutes.
Nearby events, including the When We Were Young festival and the upcoming Formula One Grand Prix, complicated travel around the convention center.
Twitch reports that in 2022 over 70% of its viewers were between 18 and 34, and most Las Vegas venues are 21+.
Steve Saylor, a blind gamer and disability advocate, said he struggled to get around Las Vegas even with rideshares.
Moni (Monistreams) posted frustrations on Twitch's UserVoice feedback forum, saying people were stuck in Ubers or walking an hour instead of being at the con.
Attendees suggested returning to San Diego or hosting both West Coast and East Coast TwitchCons; VidCon recently launched a second convention in Baltimore, Maryland.
